threads.body: This inheritance change is what preserves chunk timing for `fetch_response`, but no test asserts that a streamed `FetchResponseInvocation` emits both timing metrics; the new positive wrapper test only exercises `handler.inference`, and the Google fetch tests do not assert these metrics. Add a fetch-response regression test that checks both metric names and their operation/provider attribute value types.

This base is intentionally internal and is not re-exported, but its unprefixed name makes it look public. The util API convention requires module-private objects to start with `_`; please rename it to `_StreamedResponseInvocation` and update the two private imports/subclasses so it does not become an accidental API commitment.

This comment omits `fetch_response`, even though `FetchResponseInvocation` now implements `_on_stream_chunk` and the PR explicitly preserves timing for it. Since fetch-response performs no inference, describing the condition as inference-only is inaccurate.

This issue also appears on line 491 of the same file.

threads.body: Should `fetch_response` be excluded here too? The current semconv defines these chunk-timing histograms as client inference metrics, while `fetch_response` explicitly performs no inference. Keeping this inheritance means streamed response retrievals still emit inference-only metrics. I think only `InferenceInvocation` should use this timing base.
can we check invocation instance type instread? Or have some class-level flag on invocations indicating when to record streaming metrics (and attribute) ?
